topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the course structure, and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Intrinsic, genetic, and environmental determinants of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises from the interplay of intrinsic cellular errors, inherited genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures demonstrated by epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Molecular and cellular mechanisms of environmental carcinogens and promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological, physical, and chemical agents drive malignancy through direct DNA damage, xenobiotic metabolism, tumor promotion, and tissue- or stage-specific host susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro approaches used to detect and evaluate the carcinogenic potential of environmental agents.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a discussion of everyday risk-versus-benefit decisions regarding carcinogen exposure and summarizes the central themes.
